# Agent workflow: stages and roles

<!-- practices:learn:start (generated by scripts/practices/practices.py; do not edit) -->
**Learn this:** [Retire checks](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/retire-checks/index.html) (explainer with a [quiz](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/retire-checks/index.html#quiz)); [Life of a request](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/request-life/index.html) (explainer with a [quiz](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/request-life/index.html#quiz)). Learner path: Working with agents, step 2.
<!-- practices:learn:end -->

HQ's flow is the same for a one-line fix and a rollout; only the size of each stage changes. Roles are lanes by tier,
not personas ([subagents-and-context.md](subagents-and-context.md#pick-the-cheapest-tier-that-works)).

## Roles

| Role | Does | Tier | Never |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `supervisor` | Picks work, writes the item, briefs, verifies, lands what workers did not ([Who lands](#who-lands); `/fleet`) | Opus (judgment), Sonnet for routine | Edits what another session owns; trusts a report |
| `coordinator` | One repo's autopilot coordinator of builders: picks, reviews, lands | Sonnet, Opus for design | Lands two branches at once |
| `autopilot` | A session that pulls a repo's backlog on its own | Sonnet | Widens a scope the maintainer set |
| `worker` | Implements one item in its own worktree, runs the gate, lands it with `repos-ship` when the brief says `land: self`, otherwise pushes the branch; reports; ends (a subagent worker is stored as `builder-subagent`) | Sonnet | Lands without `land: self`; weakens a gate; widens scope; idles after the hand-back |
| `reviewer` | Applies named [lenses](review-lenses.md) to the diff, returns findings with `file:line` | Higher tier than the worker, or the local model / Junie for a cheap second read | Edits the code under review |
| `researcher` | Read-only research and fact-gathering with `file:line`, a note as output; the research pass on `idea` items ([continuous-work.md](continuous-work.md)) | Local model, Junie, Haiku | Changes files |
| `designer` | The design pass on `design` items: options, a recommendation, a `maintainer-question` with a default ([continuous-work.md](continuous-work.md)) | Opus; Fable only on request | Builds; waits for the answer |
| `keeper` | A timer or no-LLM tick (fleet keeper, queue) | none | Starts work beyond its nudge |

`kind` (`session` or `subagent`) and `surface` (`desktop`, `tmux-cli`, `remote-control`, `cloud`) are separate registry
fields, not roles. The stored value `builder-subagent` is the alias for a worker of kind `subagent`; renaming it waits
for a major flow bump.

A role is data, not prose: one file per role (model, effort, tools, permission mode, practice pages, never-list,
hand-back lines) that tools read; the subagent roles also generate `.claude/agents/<role>.md`, so the harness enforces
tools and model (`just cc-roles`; a hook fails on drift). Reasoning:
[roles for agents](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/docs/research/2026-11-08-roles-for-agents.md).

## Stages

The picture of this flow, with its decisions, loops and lanes, is the Atlas `workflow` workspace in [docs/architecture/workflow/](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/docs/architecture/workflow/atlas.yaml) (HQ web: Diagrams; locally `just docs-atlas-open workflow`); the table below is the text of the same stages.

| # | Stage | Output | Check before the next stage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Request | A backlog item, at once, if not finished in the same session | The whole request is in it ("whole requirement" lens) |
| 2 | Preflight | Pace, capacity, overlaps, tier per start ([supervisor-preflight.md](supervisor-preflight.md)) | `/preflight` ran; "slow down" starts nothing |
| 3 | Plan (size `l`, or unclear or cross-cutting) | The item's Done when, Plan, Not in scope, Open ([spec-driven-work.md](spec-driven-work.md)) | The premise can be proven false; every Done-when line is testable; no open question |
| 4 | Build | A branch with small commits, gate green | The worker's own gate run |
| 5 | Review | Findings per lens | `just q-integrity` on the branch; a report is a claim: the supervisor checks it with git and `repos-landed` ([who lands](#who-lands)) |
| 6 | Land | Merged, pushed, main checkout pulled, item deleted | Gate on the merged result, every hook ran, none skipped for a missing tool ([quality-gate.md](quality-gate.md#every-step-ran-or-the-gate-is-not-green)) |
| 6a | Release (only when this landing is a release; a package, tool or paper-code repo) | One commit that bumps the single version source, a dated changelog entry, then the annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` | `just repos-conformance run <repo>` shows `version-one-source` ok; the built `--version` / About print `X.Y.Z (sha)` without `-dirty` ([release step](releases-and-versions.md#the-release-step)) |
| 7 | Retro | A practice, a guard or a chore change | Reusable lessons go to `practices/`, the repo keeps a short rule ([chore](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/docs/CHORES.md)) |
| 7a | Follow-up | The next item pulled (`backlog_next claim:true`); every follow-up noticed filed as a backlog item or a session card at once, never only a sentence in the report | Nothing left only in the report; then the sync below for the next task |
| 8 | Retire | The session archived, `retired <id>` in the ledger | The four checks of [Retire a session](#retire-a-session) |

### When a stage fails

The table is the happy path. Each failure has one loop back, never a stop and never a skip. The same flow drawn with
its decisions and loops is the Atlas model in [docs/architecture/workflow](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/docs/architecture/workflow)
(`atlas render workflow docs/architecture/workflow --format svg`). The table is generated from the model's elements
tagged `failure` (`just docs-atlas-failures --write`; the `atlas-check` hook fails when it is stale), so edit the loop
in `docs/architecture/workflow/elements/f.NN.yaml`, not here:

<!-- atlas:failures begin -->

| Where | Failure | Loop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 Build, 6 Land | Gate red | Read the first failing step, fix on the branch, rerun that step, then the full gate on the merged tree. An e2e that fails on an unrelated branch (a version bump only) is rerun once; a second failure is a finding, filed as an item |
| 6 Land | `EXIT=143` or "killed" | Not a test failure: wait for room (`machine-wait --for heavy`), rerun ([Gate results](agent-landing.md#gate-results-and-landing)) |
| 6 Land | `repos-ship` refuses ("network down", API unreachable) | Check the host once by `curl`; reachable: run `repos-ship` again (a heavy job, so not under power saving); still down: leave the branch pushed, queue the ship, say so in the round table |
| 6 Land | Power level `saving` or "slow down" | `land: self` becomes push and wait; the supervisor starts `repos-ship` when `cc-power check --kind heavy` exits 0 |
| 5 Review, 6 Land | Hand-back and git disagree (sha unknown, not pushed, not on `origin/main`) | The hand-back goes back to the worker; it is never logged as landed ([Who lands](#who-lands)) |
| 5 Review | Findings | Fix on the branch, re-review only the changed lens, then back to 6 |
| 6 Land | The landing removed the worker's worktree | Run the repo's own post-landing checks before `repos-ship`'s finish, or leave them to the supervisor's `repos-landed` and `repos-conformance` |
| 8 Retire | A retire check fails | Name it in the ledger, do the missing step (land, retro, record), check again next round |
| any | The worker ends waiting on the user with a green gate and no landing | Sessions-continue style nudge with the end state; if the repo's AGENTS.md holds the change for review, file a manual action instead |
<!-- atlas:failures end -->

### Optional: review by a stronger model

An opt-in step between 4 Build and 6 Land for risky work: UI/UX, security, large or risky diffs, or when the maintainer
asks. Opt in per item with `review: stronger` in the item's front matter or a line in the brief; it is never the
default.

1. **Plan check first:** `just cc-usage`. Never on "SLOW DOWN"; a tight pace means the lens review by the
   supervisor instead.
2. **Reviewer:** a read-only Opus or Fable subagent started through the Agent tool with `model` (a session-start tool
   that caps the model at the caller's own would run it on the wrong tier). It edits nothing and returns the fixed
   report template of [review-lenses.md](review-lenses.md#review-by-a-stronger-model).
3. **Findings become one backlog item** (in the repo it concerns), not a chat list.
4. **The implementing, cheaper model fixes them** (the builder or a Sonnet worker), not the reviewer.
5. **The supervisor runs `just q-integrity`** and, when it lands the branch itself (`land: supervisor`), the gate once
   on the merged tree; the report is a claim ([who lands](#who-lands)).

**Sync at the start and the end of a task** (details in
[git-worktrees-and-autoland.md](git-worktrees-and-autoland.md)): at the start `git fetch` and branch from
`origin/main` (a session resumed after hours fetches again before it continues); at the end merge `origin/main`, gate,
push, then `git -C <primary> pull --ff-only`. Briefs for workers and subagents repeat this line.

Land with `just repos-ship <repo> <branch>` (merges main into the branch, runs the gate, lands, finishes, pulls; one result
line). After a landing by other means, clean up with `just repos-finish <repo> <branch>` (it proves the landing, then removes the clean
worktree and deletes the branch locally and on origin; [prepared-commands.md](prepared-commands.md)), never a
hand-written `worktree remove` / `branch -D` chain.

### Who lands

Landing follows the brief: `land: self` (default for size `s`/`m` with a green gate) means the worker runs `just repos-ship`; `land: supervisor` means it pushes and ends. Details and gate results: [agent-landing.md](agent-landing.md). A hand-back is small and lands within the day; clean branches go through one batch gate ([landing lane](agent-landing.md#landing-lane)).

**The gate runs once per landing.** With `land: self` the worker's own gate on the merged tree is the gate; the supervisor
verifies with git and `just repos-landed` and runs no second gate (it would double the load and race the landing). With
`land: supervisor` the supervisor runs the gate once on the merged tree before it lands.

## Know the owner of a file

Before you edit a file you do not know, ask the context map who owns it: the `atlas_where` MCP tool (or `atlas query where <path> docs/architecture/contexts`) answers in a few lines with the owning context, its relations, the words it owns and its links; `atlas_list` names the contexts. A path no context claims answers `unowned`, which is a gap in `paths:` to fix, not an error. `atlas check` prints the share of tracked code files that a context owns and fails below 88 %.

## Retire a session

A finished session is archived with its retro, after its four checks (landed, retro, archive, record). The checks and the flow: [agent-retire.md](agent-retire.md); the picture is the `retire` view of the Atlas `workflow` workspace.

- **Detach, then archive.** A session with a Remote Control client is refused by `archive_session`: call `detach_session <local_id>` (or turn Remote Control off) first; `cc-fleet-round retire --apply` prints both calls.
- **Keep.** A session the maintainer wants alive even when idle (the coordinator, long-running autopilots) is marked `just cc-fleet-ledger session set HANDLE --set keep=true --set keep_reason=TEXT`; `retire` skips it as `kept (<reason>)`, so `--apply` never lists it. Retire a kept session only when the maintainer says so in chat.
- **No new item while retiring.** The `.closing` marker (written by `cc-retire`) makes the Stop hook claim nothing; a lease the hook took after the branch's last commit is not counted by the ship's "leased item not closed" check.

## Guards by stage

| Stage | Guard |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | `PreToolUse` preflight gate ([supervisor-preflight.md](supervisor-preflight.md)) |
| 4 | Destructive-command guard ([agent-security.md](agent-security.md#command-guard)) |
| 5 | `just q-integrity` ([review-lenses.md](review-lenses.md#gate-integrity)), `just q-check` |
| 6 | Landing rules of the repo; push every commit |

Read the gate's exit code (`echo $?`, or the completion notice's status) before a push: a log that scrolled past is not a
pass. A failure is fixed or reported, never pushed over; an unrelated flaky test is re-run once under low load and named
in the report.

## Periodic self-analysis

Every few hours of a long run and in the weekly Retro chore, answer six measured questions from data and make one change per finding: [agent-retire.md](agent-retire.md#periodic-self-analysis).

## A fixed bug is reported again

Before looking for a missed code path, compare times: the commit that fixed it, the build time of the image or binary
that runs, and the container's start time (`docker inspect`, `docker ps`: "Up N hours" keeps serving the old code).
A long-running service only changes when it is rebuilt and restarted, so a landing that does not redeploy leaves
the reported bug in place. Reproduce against the code first (a parser run on the maintainer's files), then against the
running build; say in the report which of the two still fails. A deploy to a machine that is the only one in use is
a production change: it needs the maintainer's instruction, or goes to a `manual-action` issue with the exact commands.

Related, for a migration with a frozen oracle: a new golden needs the update switch of its test (`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`),
a recorder names the tag that retires its oracle, and a background gate must `cd` into its worktree inside the
command (the launcher shell's directory is not the gate's).

Reading a gate result: a commit made while the gate waits for the lock supersedes it (`EXIT=75`), and a hook
formatter's uncommitted edits or an old `/tmp` log can pass for a result. Check the log's mtime and grep for `GATE OK`,
or use `hq q-gate-result`. Run `git push` and the gate as separate commands: in `git push && gate` a failed push (a
GitHub 500) silently skips the gate. New fixture files also need the goldens list regenerated (`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`).

## Check the premise before building

A request can describe something that is already done or cannot be reproduced. In one round of six UI requests two were
already built (a tool a maintainer expected "moved" already lived under Tools; a task-assignment inbox with a badge
existed) and two bugs (a wheel landing at the wrong angle, a vanished desktop view) did not reproduce at the stated sizes.

- First `grep` the code and the changelog for the feature, and reproduce the bug in the real app at the reported size,
  before writing a backlog body that assumes the premise.
- Premise false: delete the item in a docs-only commit that says so, and tell the maintainer in one line what you found
  (and what label or entry point may have misled them); do not build a duplicate.
- Bug not reproduced: harden the likely cause only when it is cheap and test-pinned, and say plainly it was not reproduced.
- A formatter run over a whole folder reformats files you did not touch; format the files you changed, stage by name,
  and discard stray reformatting before the landing check.

## Brief rules: search main first, hand back after a finished gate

Two rules for every worker brief and hand-back (observed 2026-11-12: three autopilots were typed the same item, and
hand-backs arrived with "gate did not finish"):

- **Search `main` first.** Before building, the worker greps the default branch (and `git log -S`/`git log --grep` for
  the item id) for the feature, the file or a branch that already does it; found means the item is done or a duplicate,
  so report that instead of building ([Check the premise](#check-the-premise-before-building)). A worker also claims the
  item (`backlog_claim`) so a second session does not pick it.
- **A hand-back needs a finished gate.** The hand-back names the gate command and its result (PASS or the failing hook)
  from a run that completed on the branch's final commit. A killed or still-running gate is not a result: the worker
  waits for the completion notice, reruns if it was killed, and only then hands back. The supervisor rejects a hand-back
  without one and does not ship it (`repos-dod` shows the line). It also needs an empty `git status --short` line and
  `also fails on main: yes|no` beside any failing test; `repos-dod --handback` fails without them and prints the
  `git worktree remove` command for a verified subagent worktree.

## The Retire line

The Definition of Done hand-back block ends with one machine-readable line, written only after the branch is pushed
and its gate finished:

```text
Retire: ready branch=<branch> sha=<head sha> lessons=<practices page | item id | none-needed>
```

`cc-fleet-round retire` (and `cc-retire`, `retire --session <id>`) read it as the input of the git checks only: the
`sha` must be on origin's default branch (a `land: supervisor` hand-back is "pushed only" until the supervisor lands
it) and the `branch` must be landed or gone, so a wrong or local-only sha fails `landed`. When the line is present, it replaces
the scan of every sha and branch name in the note (a stale name no longer blocks). The line is a claim, never proof:
git decides. It does not replace the `Lessons saved:` line, which the retro check still reads; `lessons=` repeats it for
the supervisor's table. Use `-` for a value that does not apply.

A child session retires itself: the `retire-self` Stop hook (`scripts/claude/hooks/retire-self.py`) runs
`fleet-round.py retire --session <id>` when a child's turn ends. If all four checks pass, it writes the hand-back
as a `self-retire` line in the fleet ledger and blocks the stop once, telling the session to call `archive_session self`
and then `retire --record-archived <local_id>`. It stays silent for the maintainer's and supervisor sessions, when a
`.closing` marker exists, after its one block, and when any check fails.
